title: PTE Listening: Tasks & the Write-from-Dictation Goldmine
summary: Summarize Spoken Text, Write from Dictation, Highlight Incorrect Words and more — where the high-value listening marks hide.

nodes.label: Highlight Incorrect Words
nodes.note: Click words that differ from audio

nodes.label: Select Missing Word
nodes.note: Choose the word that ends the clip

chunks.heading: Write from Dictation — the biggest ROI in the test
chunks.body: You hear a **short sentence once** and **type it exactly**. It scores **listening AND writing**, and it carries a lot of weight for a 15-second task — so it's the single highest-value listening item to master. **Every correctly-spelled word in the right place earns marks.**
chunks.realExample: Trick: as the sentence plays, jot the first letters or key words on the erasable notepad, then reconstruct the full sentence from them before typing. Even 6 of 8 words correct scores well.
chunks.memoryHook: Write from Dictation pays double and pays big. Catch keywords, rebuild, type.

chunks.heading: Summarize Spoken Text — 50 to 70 words
chunks.body: Listen to a recording and write a **50–70 word summary** (scores **listening + writing**). Take notes on the **main idea plus 2–3 supporting points** while listening, then shape them into a few clean sentences inside the word range.
chunks.realExample: Note-taking shorthand: main point at the top, then bullet the supports with arrows. Your notes, not your memory, become the summary — you can't replay the audio.
chunks.memoryHook: Main idea + 2–3 supports, 50–70 words. Notes now, sentences after.

chunks.heading: Highlight Incorrect Words & Select Missing Word — read while you listen
chunks.body: **Highlight Incorrect Words**: a transcript is on screen and you **click the words that differ** from what the speaker says. **Select Missing Word**: the audio cuts out and you **choose the word that completes it**. Both need you to **track the transcript in real time**.
chunks.realExample: In Highlight Incorrect Words, keep your cursor moving along the text as the audio plays — the moment a printed word doesn't match your ear, click it, then keep tracking. Don't stop to second-guess.
chunks.memoryHook: Follow the text with your eyes as the voice speaks. Mismatch → click → keep moving.

chunks.heading: The multiple-choice items — same caution as Reading
chunks.body: Listening also has **single-answer and multiple-answer MCQs** and **Highlight Correct Summary** (pick the paragraph that best matches the clip — scores **listening + reading**). On multiple-answer items, **wrong picks lose marks**, so choose only what you're sure of.
chunks.realExample: Highlight Correct Summary: eliminate the option with a detail the audio never mentioned — wrong summaries usually add or twist one fact.
chunks.memoryHook: Kill the summary with the invented detail. Multiple-answer: only what you're sure of.

recall.q: Why is Write from Dictation considered the highest-ROI listening task?
recall.a: It scores both listening and writing, carries significant weight, and every correctly-placed, correctly-spelled word earns marks — for a very short task.

recall.q: What is the word range for Summarize Spoken Text?
What do you do in Highlight Incorrect Words?
recall.a: Click the words in the on-screen transcript that differ from what the speaker actually says, tracking the text as the audio plays.

recall.q: Which listening tasks also feed your writing score?
recall.a: Summarize Spoken Text and Write from Dictation.

recall.q: How should you approach a 'multiple answers' listening question?
recall.a: Select only the options you're confident about, because wrong selections lose marks.
